title: Stoichiometric Relationships Adventure 2: Gas laws and ideal gas equation
welcome_lead: Today you'll use pV=nRT and find the molar volume of an ideal gas.
meta_desc: Chemistry — ideal gas law pV=nRT, molar volume 22.7 dm³ at STP, gas calculations.
final_note: You learned pV=nRT links 4 variables, molar volume is 22.7 dm³ mol⁻¹ at STP (100 kPa, 273 K), and gas volumes follow mole ratios.

walkthroughs.body_html:
pV = nRT

- p in Pa (or kPa × 1000)
- V in m³ (or dm³ × 10⁻³)
- n in mol
- T in K (always!)
- R = 8.31 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹

At STP (100 kPa, 273 K), 1 mol = 22.7 dm³.

For a fixed amount of gas: p₁V₁/T₁ = p₂V₂/T₂

Example: 100 cm³ at 25°C, 100 kPa. Heat to 100°C at constant p:
V₂ = V₁T₂/T₁ = 100 × 373/298 = 125 cm³.

International perspective: early gas laws (Boyle 1662, Charles 1787, Avogadro 1811) emerged from cross-European collaboration.

mcqs.q: What are the units of Kc for a reaction?
options: They depend on Δn (the difference between moles of gaseous/aqueous products and reactants) — Kc can be dimensionless or have units like mol dm^-3.
Kc always has units of mol dm^-3.
The ions start as solid elements before being assembled into the lattice.
Kc is always dimensionless.

mcqs.q: Does adding a catalyst change the value of Kc?
options: A catalyst increases Kc by favouring product formation.
No — a catalyst speeds up forward and reverse reactions equally, so Kc is unchanged.
The ions start as solid elements before being assembled into the lattice.
A catalyst decreases Kc by stabilising the reactants.

mcqs.q: What state are the ions in when defining lattice enthalpy of formation?
options: The ions start as solid elements before being assembled into the lattice.
A catalyst decreases Kc by stabilising the reactants.
The ions are in aqueous solution before forming the lattice.
Gaseous ions — lattice enthalpy is the energy change when one mole of solid ionic compound forms from its constituent ions in the GAS phase.
